name: Galio
notes: Opens with Hero's Entrance (R) at t=0, self-targeted: Galio counts as his own ally for the ult's landing-spot designation, since a fight with no allies otherwise leaves it uncastable. The 2.75s channel blocks basic attacks and every other cast, and the impact damage lands the instant the channel ends.

Colossal Smash's unresolved cooldown-multiplier term is read as a flat 5 seconds between empowered-attack procs (not shortened by ability haste, since it is an innate, not a basic ability). It is cut short by 3 seconds, down to the current time, whenever Q, E, a W recast, or R's impact lands on the dummy (once per cast); Galio is assumed to start the fight with it already charged.

Colossal Smash's bonus magic resistance ratio, and Hero's Entrance's identical ratio, are applied against the TARGET/Galio's TOTAL magic resistance because the engine's stat sheet exposes only total MR, not a base/bonus split; this overstates their contribution by roughly base MR times the ratio and is flagged as an approximation.
Only Colossal Smash's AD-ratio portion is dealt as crit-eligible, per the wiki; every other instance (its base+AP+MR portion, Q, E, W, R) cannot critically strike.

Winds of War is always cast directly onto the dummy so both windblasts converge immediately: the gust deals its damage on cast, then the tornado ticks 4 times every 0.5s over 2s for a percent of the dummy's maximum health each tick. The monster damage cap on the tornado is not applied since the dummy counts as an enemy champion, not a monster.

Justice Punch's dash damage uses the full champion-damage value (not the 80% non-champion value) since the dummy counts as an enemy champion; the short step-back-then-dash is abstracted into its 0.4s cast, landing the damage on cast, same as the reference approach for short dashes.

Shield of Durand is always charged to its 1.25s damage/radius/taunt scaling cap before being manually recast right at that mark, since 1.25s is small next to its 14-18s cooldown and always yields the maximum (x3 minimum) recast damage; the following 0.4s post-recast lockout blocks attacks and casts, per the wiki, and the cooldown itself starts on the initial cast.
Colossal Smash's documented (and bug-flagged) double application of on-hit effects to its primary target is not modeled; on-hit items apply once per attack as usual.
Mana costs are not modeled: nothing in this kit binds within a 15s fight at level 16.
